children: President Trump on Saturday said he has approved new fuel economy standards for cars and trucks, adding that he has eliminated an electric vehicle mandate signed by former President Biden.

"These new Standards will take the waste out of building cars in America," he wrote on Truth Social. "That means LOWER PRICES, saving families thousands on a new, beautiful, and safe car — Far better than the Environmental Monsters that we were building heretofore."
Trump added that under his administration, more than $100B is being invested in American automobile manufacturing.
A Biden 2021 executive order aimed to have half of all new vehicle sales in the US electric by 2030.

In late August, Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy said that the administration would soon unveil a "common-sense fuel economy standard because we want ​Detroit to build cars that Americans want to buy—not cars that Democrats want Washington ​to build."

In December 2025, the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration proposed a fleetwide average of 34.5 miles (ca. 56 kilometers) per gallon by 2031. Biden had called for 50.4 miles (ca. 81 kilometers) per gallon.

While NHTSA projected its proposal would lead to savings of $930 per vehicle, it would add 100 billion gallons of fuel consumption through 2050, increase carbon dioxide emissions by 5%, and boost fuel spending by $185B, according to a Reuters report.

title: Trump OKs new fuel economy standards, ends Biden EV mandate
